events.title: Saturday Night Massacre
events.description: During the Watergate scandal, President Richard Nixon ordered the firing of Special Prosecutor Archibald Cox. Attorney General Elliot Richardson and Deputy Attorney General William Ruckelshaus resigned rather than carry out the order, and Solicitor General Robert Bork carried out the dismissal.
events.significance: The event intensified public and congressional outrage over Watergate, sharply increased calls for impeachment, and contributed to Nixon's resignation in 1974.

events.title: Sydney Opera House Opened
events.description: Queen Elizabeth II officially opened the Sydney Opera House in Australia, designed by Danish architect Jørn Utzon, after a construction period of about 14 years marked by controversy and cost overruns.
events.significance: The building became an iconic symbol of Australia and was later designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007.

events.title: Return of General MacArthur to the Philippines
events.description: American forces led by General Douglas MacArthur landed on Leyte in the Philippines, beginning the campaign to liberate the islands from Japanese occupation. MacArthur waded ashore, fulfilling his 1942 promise 'I shall return.'
events.significance: The landing marked a major turning point in the Pacific War and led to the Battle of Leyte Gulf, one of the largest naval battles in history.

events.title: Battle of Navarino
events.description: A combined British, French, and Russian fleet destroyed the Ottoman and Egyptian fleet at Navarino Bay during the Greek War of Independence.
events.significance: The victory was decisive in securing Greek independence from the Ottoman Empire.

events.title: Birth of John Dewey
events.description: American philosopher and educational reformer John Dewey was born in Burlington, Vermont. He became a leading figure in pragmatism and progressive education.
events.significance: Dewey's ideas profoundly influenced education systems, democratic theory, and philosophy in the 20th century.
